title: Circuit + Simulation-driven VPC health reconciler and autorepair workflow
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Build an automated reconciler that detects common Private (VPC) healthcheck failures, runs controlled remediation actions via Terraform/IaC where safe, and validates fixes with synthetic simulations and canary checks before wide remediation. The goal is to reduce mean time to repair for customer VPC probe failures while ensuring zero-blast-radius operations through circuit breakers and simulation-driven decisioning.
background: We continue to see a class of Private health incidents where probe failures are caused by transient network policy drift, expired TLS certs for the agent, node agent crashes after upgrades, and occasional terraform state drift for auto-provisioned components. Existing runbooks are manual and varied across on-call responders. We need an operator + playbook that codifies safe automated remediation patterns and a simulation harness to exercise repairs in staging before production.
proposed_solution: Introduce a reconciler service (stateless controller) that: 1) subscribes to VPC probe health metrics and synthetic probe failures; 2) classifies failure root-candidates (network, cert, agent-process, infra instance); 3) runs a dry-run Terraform plan to compute repair changes; 4) uses a decision policy (simulation score + safety gates) to pick an action: do-nothing (alert), restart agent, rotate certs, recreate node, or schedule operator-assisted repair. Key safety mechanisms: rate-limited repairs, concurrency limits by customer, per-repair canary simulation in an isolated replica VPC (where available), a global circuit breaker to stop auto-remediation if overall false-positive rate > threshold, and an audit trail (immutable) logged to S3/KMS. Integrates with existing IaC modules (terraform/private-node, terraform/vpc-probes) and Console rollout APIs for canary watches.
acceptance_criteria: Reconciler can detect and classify at least 4 common failure signatures with >= 85% precision in test harness
Dry-run Terraform plans are generated for detected drift and surfaced in the Console UI as proposed fixes
Automated remediation can be executed in canary mode and validated with synthetic probes with pass/fail signals
Circuit breaker prevents >1 repair per customer per 6 hours and global auto-remediation can be disabled via Console toggle
Full audit trail (who/what/when) is recorded for every automated action and surfaced in the incident timeline
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Integration tests against terraform modules in local CI (unit + plan diffs)
Phase 1: Deploy reconciler to staging and enable canary simulation harness using synthetic VPC copies
Phase 2: Beta with 5 low-risk customers (opt-in) with auto-repair disabled, only suggested actions in Console
Phase 3: Enable automated canary repairs for beta customers with human approval fallback
Phase 4: Gradual rollout to production with circuit breakers, monitor FP rate and customer impact for 2 weeks before wider enablement
test_plan: Unit tests for classifier models and signature matching
Integration test: terraform plan/apply in a sandboxed account with state locking
Chaos simulation: inject probe failures (network ACL, cert expiry, agent crash) and assert reconciler chooses correct action
Canary validation: run synthetic probes against canary VPC and measure post-repair success within 5 minutes
Long-run: run reconciler in dry mode for 7 days against production telemetry and compare suggested actions to historical on-call fixes
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: false-positive repairs causing customer disruption. Mitigation: default to suggested actions; automated applies require two safety gates (canary pass + low FP trending) unless explicit opt-in

Risk: Terraform plan drift could accidentally remove customer config. Mitigation: run plan in read-only mode first, require 'apply intent' signed by operator or customer-managed approval for destructive changes
Risk: secrets leakage from state files. Mitigation: use remote state with encryption, KMS keys per-customer, never persist plaintext in logs
Risk: large-scale repair loop. Mitigation: global rate limiter + per-customer token bucket + exponential backoff for repeated failures
runbook: Triage: Confirm probe failure with Console synthetic probe timeline and correlate with agent logs (private-agent.log) via log-id
Classify: Use reconciler UI to view classification and dry-run terraform plan. If classification uncertain, tag incident 'manual-review' and notify SRE rotation
Canary: For automation-enabled customers, run canary repair against an isolated replica VPC and wait up to 10 minutes for synthetic probe to succeed
Apply: If canary passes and safety gates are green, execute terraform apply with state lock and record run-id. Monitor apply and watch post-apply probes for 15 minutes
Rollback: If post-apply probes fail or errors > 3%, trigger automated rollback via saved terraform state snapshot and mark repair as failed
Escalate: If unable to reconcile or repeated failures, open a customer incident and run manual remediation checklist: network debug (tcpdump), cert rotation, agent debug logs, node replacement
Post-incident: Attach audit trail, terraform run logs, canary results, and create follow-up ticket for module fix if root cause is IaC bug
automation_details: Terraform: reuse modules terraform/private-node and terraform/vpc-probes. All automated applies run with -auto-approve only after canary success and approval flags
State: remote state locked in s3 backend with dynamodb locks. All plans executed with -refresh and saved plan artifacts for audit
Simulation harness: uses VPC replica snapshots (where available) or a simulated network stack to exercise repairs without touching production resources
Operator: reconciler exposes a dry-run endpoint, a queued apply flow, and an audit webhook that posts to Console and Slack
Safety: global circuit breaker implemented in reconciler, configurable thresholds stored in Console config (rate, FP threshold, per-customer concurrency)
monitoring_and_alerting: New metrics: reconciler.suggestions.count, reconciler.applies.count, reconciler.fp_rate, reconciler.canary_success_rate
Dashboards: per-customer panel for suggested vs applied actions and mean time to fix
Alerts: PagerDuty if reconciler.applies fails > 5 in 15m or fp_rate > 20% over 1h
Audit logs: immutable run artifacts retained 90 days with KMS encryption
postmortem_and_rollback: If a repair causes regression, reconcile will auto-rollback using the saved terraform plan snapshot. Engineers will run postmortem within 3 working days and include canary results, FP analysis, and module changes
Follow-ups may include increased simulation coverage, classifier retraining with missed examples, and Terraform module hardening
